---
title: "Env.SetInt"
description: "Set an int value by key in the Env store."
---

Set the `int` value for `key`. Silent no-op if the pool is full (256 entries).

## Signature

```enforce
static proto native void SetInt(string key, int v);
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| key | `string` | The key to write. |
| v | `int` | The int value to store. |

## Behavior

The store is locked; writes are serialized. If `key` previously held a non-Int kind, the kind is replaced by Int (the old value is lost). If the pool already has 256 entries, the write is silently dropped — there is no error return and no diagnostic.

## Edge cases

- Writing past the 256-entry cap is a silent no-op. Use [Env.Erase](./erase) or [Env.Clear](./clear) to free space, and use [Env.AlreadyRan](./alreadyran) to avoid fabricating per-run keys.
- No way to distinguish a successful write from a dropped write from script. If you need to know, [Env.Has](./has) tells you the key was touched before.

## Example

```enforce
Env.SetInt("counter", Env.GetInt("counter") + 1);
```
